prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Fouling of ultrafiltration membranes in protein-rich bioprocess streams is driven by protein conformation and aggregation state, with these mechanisms characterized through resistance-in-series diagnostic frameworks and surface analysis.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03384","field":"abstract","quote":"protein conformation and aggregation state in foulant deposit formation; the resistance-in-series framework"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-03376","field":"abstract","quote":"cake filtration and intermediate blocking models were fitted to experimental flux–volume data"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Pre-treatment of fermentation broths with protease prior to ultrafiltration was evaluated as a fouling mitigation strategy, with limiting flux increased by 38% compared with untreated broth at a hydrolysis degree of 16%.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03380","field":"abstract","quote":"Pre-treatment of a model fermentation broth with a commercial serine protease was evaluated as a fouling mitigation strategy"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-03380","field":"abstract","quote":"At a hydrolysis degree of 16%, the limiting flux increased by 38% compared with untreated broth"}]}]}
